Empieza | Starbie Session #1
----------------------------

Introduction/Introducion
-------------------------
Hi, and welcome to my first log regarding the starbie project. I go by DesdeDerrota per my github name, and while I have done a few projects here or there, the idea of creating a board is still a very new thing for me.
This is why, during this project, I hope to really grow, and what better way to do that then with a starbie?


Files/Archivos
----------------
To begin my first session, today, I opened up the docs at 10 pm est, and started the process of creating a repository for this project, downloading and reading the documentation files, and the added, but very useful step of
creating a folder for my HackClub creations. After this was done, I started the download of KiCad to my computer to start working on the schematics. This took about 15 mins, so I left to do other things
(7 mins elapsed working so far).

Resuming at 1:09 AM in the morning, I finalized the download on my device and finished the setup. Two videos by Kody Rogers on Youtube helped me install the libraries, though I fiddled a little bit.


Designing The Board/Desenando El Bordo
--------------------------------------

I started work on the board, though got a little side tracked as by the time I got to this point, I downloaded the footprint library but not the symbol library, and couldn't find the XIAO-ESP32 board. After a small
revelation, I thought to maybe download the symbol library too. After fiddling around with my computer and it's infernal files, I got it to work. I started working on designing at 1:36. But there was a problem. I have no idea
what I am doing. I got the proper ESP32 on the workspace, even got the symbols to all appear, but when I tried to link the power symbols with their arrows using the draw wires feature, which looked pretty close to the line
had by the arrow (even though I knew this probably wasn't a good idea), I had found my self in a pickle. I got stuck in the wire mode, and couldn't get out not until I managed to delete what I had so far and make a small maze
of wire. Pues, you live and you learn. 

I fiddled arond more and actually found the proper way to do this. Click the place first, and drag to make markers, or points for the line to go through. This understanding felt very good. Then came the net labels, and I 
felt lost again. A quick google search, and a 0:22 second youtube video later, I connected the dots and strove to copy the final project as close as possible, essentially spotting the difference and doing. After that was 
finished, I wondeered where I could find those x's that were on the model board, and looked across the side panel, where, wonderously enough it was there. I quickly applied the x's and then started this journal. As it is
2:10 AM, I have been working for a little over an hour. Here's my photo!

[Add Photo Here - ESP32 Board]

Starting on the next part, the buttons, I had used my new understanding to breeze through the prequisites. I even figured out how to rotate and flip the pieces with enough poking around. I think I'm gonna like this. 
I worked through the rest of the instructions on the physical side - no issues here. Very puzzle like, meditative, until I got to the assignment part, and had to type in names to get the piece I was looking for.

[Add Photo Here - Working on assignment]

The assignment step tested my patience, but I got through it, and it wasn't soo bad. One thing I have to say is that I am unsure if it is all correct. One of the assignments was autofilled, but it was in the wrong place
and named slightly differently. I chalked this up to differences in methodology, though I will check with the slack, just to be safe.

[Add Photo Here - Finished Assignment]

End/Final

All in all, I would say I got some pretty good work done. I got to get some sleep though, as it is 3:09 in the morning, (2:55 when I finished the assignment part) and I have an eventful day. Wouldn't want to be a bother,
and with that, I sign off. Goodbye entry #1, y ojala a hacer este otra vez. Ciao!
